items.text: Provide and store what is necessary to life and useful for the household.
items.quote: must either find ready to hand, or itself provide, such things necessary to life, and useful for the community of the family or state, as can be stored.

items.text: Limit the household's wealth-getting to natural provision, not unlimited accumulation.
items.quote: the art of wealth-getting which consists in household management, on the other hand, has a limit; the unlimited acquisition of wealth is not its business.

items.text: Rule those who are by nature slaves for their good, because they cannot rule themselves.
items.quote: the lower sort are by nature slaves, and it is better for them as for all inferiors that they should be under the rule of a master.
items.conflict: Natural slavery denies that all people are made in God's image and that in Christ there is neither slave nor free (Gen 1:27; Gal 3:28).

items.text: Rule over your wife, for the male is by nature superior and the female is by nature inferior.
items.quote: the male is by nature superior, and the female inferior; and the one rules, and the other is ruled; this principle, of necessity, extends to all mankind.
items.conflict: Scripture makes husband and wife joint heirs of grace and one flesh; headship is not female inferiority or being ruled as an inferior nature (Gen 1:27; 1 Pet 3:7; Eph 5:21-33).

items.text: Serve your master as a living instrument of action, wholly belonging to him.
items.quote: the slave is not only the slave of his master, but wholly belongs to him
items.conflict: Treating a person as chattel contradicts 1 Corinthians 7:23 and the biblical dignity of all persons.

items.text: Obey him and carry out the duties he orders, as nature intends for the one who serves.
items.quote: the one practicing obedience, the others exercising the authority and lordship which nature intended them to have
items.conflict: Makes some persons slaves by nature; Scripture teaches all are made in God's image and in Christ there is neither slave nor free (Gal. 3:28).

items.text: Exercise authority over him for your common good, and do not abuse it, since his good and yours are one.
items.quote: The abuse of this authority is injurious to both; for the interests of part and whole, of body and soul, are the same
items.conflict: Treats a person as a part of the master's body; masters must give servants what is right and fair (Col. 4:1).

items.text: In the natural relation, be his friend and seek a common interest with him, not mere force.
items.quote: where the relation of master and slave between them is natural they are friends and have a common interest
items.conflict: Grounds friendship in natural slavery; Christian love treats servants as brothers in Christ (Philemon 16).

items.text: Order the things nature supplies for your household, as a weaver uses wool, knowing what is good and serviceable.
items.quote: the duty of the manager of a household, who has to order the things which nature supplies

items.text: Consider the health of your household, but leave the practice of medicine to physicians.
items.quote: from one point of view the master of the house and the ruler of the state have to consider about health

items.text: Learn which livestock and crops are profitable and where, and manage them for the household's provision.
items.quote: A man ought to know which of these pay better than others, and which pay best in particular places

items.text: Seek wealth only by natural household management; avoid retail trade and usury, which are unnatural.
items.quote: the former necessary and honorable, while that which consists in exchange is justly censured; for it is unnatural

items.text: Remain in the natural union of male and female for mutual existence and the continuance of the race.
items.quote: there must be a union of those who cannot exist without each other; namely, of male and female, that the race may continue

items.text: Rule the natural slave for the shared preservation of both master and slave.
items.quote: natural ruler and subject, that both may be preserved
items.conflict: Contrary to Scripture: no one is by nature a slave; all are made in God's image (Gen 1:27).

items.text: Submit as a natural slave to the master, for master and slave have the same interest.
items.quote: that which can with its body give effect to such foresight is a subject, and by nature a slave; hence master and slave have the same interest
items.conflict: Contrary to Scripture: no one is by nature a slave; all are made in God's image (Gen 1:27).

items.text: Obey the eldest who rules the family as its natural head.
items.quote: Every family is ruled by the eldest

items.text: Rule over your wife as over a free person, not as a slave.
items.quote: the rule over his children being a royal, over his wife a constitutional rule.

items.text: Accept your husband's rule, for the male is by nature fitter for command, and in marriage the inequality is permanent.
items.quote: the male is by nature fitter for command than the female
items.conflict: Wifely submission is grounded in creation order and Christ's headship, not in female natural inferiority; male and female are equally made in God's image (Gen 1:27; Eph 5:22-24).

items.text: Rule over your children as a king rules: by love and by the honor due to your age.
items.quote: The rule of a father over his children is royal, for he rules by virtue both of love and of the respect due to age

items.text: Obey your father's royal rule, for he rules by love and the honor due to age.
items.quote: The rule of a father over his children is royal

items.text: Rule over your slaves as master of the house, as part of household management.
items.quote: Of household management we have seen that there are three parts- one is the rule of a master over slaves
items.conflict: Slavery as a permanent condition conflicts with the equal dignity of all persons before God and the unity of believers in Christ (Gen 1:27; Col 3:11).

items.text: Be the source of his excellence; train him in his duties by admonition, not by command alone.
items.quote: the master ought to be the source of such excellence in the slave, and not a mere possessor of the art of mastership which trains the slave in his duties.
items.conflict: Natural slavery denies that all are image-bearers (Gen 1:27; Gal 3:28).

items.text: Cultivate enough courage and self-control not to fail in your duty.
items.quote: he will obviously require only so much virtue as will prevent him from failing in his duty through cowardice or lack of self-control.
items.conflict: Natural slavery denies that all are image-bearers (Gen 1:27; Gal 3:28).

items.text: Show your courage in commanding her, and rule with moral virtue in perfection.
items.quote: the courage of a man is shown in commanding, of a woman in obeying.

items.text: Obey him; the courage of a woman is shown in obeying.
items.quote: the courage of a man is shown in commanding, of a woman in obeying.

items.text: Keep silence, for silence is a woman's glory.
items.quote: Silence is a woman's glory
items.conflict: Women are not required to be silent as a standing glory (Prov 31:26; 1 Cor 11:5).

items.text: Train them by education with an eye to the constitution.
items.quote: children must be trained by education with an eye to the constitution

items.text: Let your virtue be relative to your parent and teacher, not to yourself alone, for you are imperfect.
items.quote: The child is imperfect, and therefore obviously his virtue is not relative to himself alone, but to the perfect man and to his teacher.

items.text: Have moral virtue in perfection, for your function demands a master artificer.
items.quote: the ruler ought to have moral virtue in perfection, for his function, taken absolutely, demands a master artificer

items.text: See that she is educated with an eye to the constitution.
items.quote: women and children must be trained by education with an eye to the constitution
